citation: Fraser WD, Goodman LS, Ackles KN, Mohn D, Pecaric M. Cardiovascular responses with standard and extended bladder coverage G-suits during rapid decompression. Aviat Space Environ Med. 1994;65(3):209–213.
locator: Subjects p. 209; Procedures and Results p. 210 (PDF p. 2)
note: Eight participants were tested in both garment conditions on separate days at least 48 h apart. The authors report no DCS symptoms and no Doppler VGE during the two test series. Practice runs are outside the measured comparison.

citation: Fraser WD, Goodman LS, Ackles KN. The effect of increased G-suit coverage on the cardiovascular effects of positive pressure breathing at 60,000 ft. Aviat Space Environ Med. 1992;63(5). Abstract 524.
note: Preliminary report with six participants and the same two garments and 60,000-ft profile. Participant linkage to the later eight-person article is unavailable. The abstract supplies no DCS or VGE count.

citation: Bancroft RW, Simmons DG. Rapid decompressions up to 60,000 feet wearing the standard oxygen mask. Aerosp Med. 1964;35(3):203–211.
note: The Brooks report describes seven rapid decompressions above 50,000 ft in five people. It reports acute oxygenation and hypoxia effects. Systematic DCS ascertainment and any DCS numerator are unavailable for this scope.

citation: Connolly DM, D’Oyly TJ, McGown AS, Lee VM. Lung volumes, pulmonary ventilation, and hypoxia following rapid decompression to 60,000 ft (18,288 m). Aviat Space Environ Med. 2013;84(6):551–559.
note: Six people made 12 rapid decompressions with two regulator conditions. One person developed severe hypoxia. The authors discuss spacing runs to limit DCS risk. A systematic DCS outcome tally and VGE assessments are unavailable.
